record.paper_title: Beam energy scan theory: Status and open questions
record.original_question: Can Color Glass Condensate initial-state modeling for heavy-ion collisions be extended to a fully three-dimensional description, and down to what collision energy do the saturation assumptions used in that framework remain valid?

evidence.quote: Extend Color Glass Condensate approaches to three dimensions and clarify down to which energy the saturation assumptions hold

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the high-energy limit of QCD, the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory describes the wavefunction of a hadron or nucleus in terms of static, large-x color sources sourcing dynamical small-x gluon fields, characterized by a saturation scale Q_s(x) that grows with energy and nuclear thickness. In its standard form, the CGC framework is formulated in the eikonal (boost-invariant) limit and is used to model the initial state of relativistic heavy-ion collisions as essentially two-dimensional in the transverse plane, with the longitudinal (rapidity) direction treated as boost-invariant.

(a) Construct an extension of the CGC initial-state framework for nucleus–nucleus collisions to a fully three-dimensional description that consistently incorporates non-eikonal corrections, finite longitudinal extent of the colliding nuclei, x-dependence (rapidity dependence) of the color sources, and the resulting non-trivial longitudinal structure of the produced gluon fields at proper time τ → 0+, in such a way that the existing 2+1-dimensional boost-invariant CGC results are recovered in the appropriate high-energy limit.

(b) Determine quantitatively the range of center-of-mass energies per nucleon pair √s_NN for which the saturation assumptions underlying the CGC (in particular Q_s ≫ Λ_QCD and the dominance of small-x gluon densities) remain self-consistent, and identify the lower energy threshold below which these assumptions break down for collisions of heavy nuclei.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of extending CGC to a fully 3D (non-boost-invariant) initial-state description, and of delineating the lowest energies at which saturation remains valid, has been actively pursued (e.g., 3D JIMWLK studies, NLO/non-eikonal CGC, work by Schenke, Schlichting, McDonald and collaborators), but no complete, universally accepted 3D CGC framework with an established lower-energy validity bound exists. The question is generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: 3D structure of the initial state in heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work develops 3D initial-state models extending CGC-based approaches beyond boost invariance, indicating the 3D extension is an active and incomplete program.
status_evidence.claim: A fully 3D CGC initial state remains under active development.

status_evidence.title: Non-eikonal corrections to the CGC
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of non-eikonal corrections show finite-energy effects that are not yet systematically incorporated into the CGC framework.
status_evidence.claim: The lower-energy limit of CGC saturation assumptions has not been definitively established.
